lowest_point_at_top_vs_safe_transit.note: no 1000 uL tool in rev B (10 / 50 / 300 uL); a p1000 tip at the fixed 243 mm nozzle height would be 15 mm below SAFE_TRANSIT_Z (5 mm above MAX_LABWARE_H, as params states)

z_backdrive.verdict: no counterbalance: the screw is self-locking for mu >= 0.088, and even at mu = 0 the unpowered motor detent (~0.020 N m) exceeds the 0.0051 N m gravity torque; verify by power-off drop test with 1.3 kg on each tool (vibration creep).

z_hard_stop_rev_g3.part: ZHS-1_z_hard_stop (CNC 6061-T6) + ISO 4026 M5x30 set screw + ISO 4035 M5 lock nut + 2 x ISO 4762 M4x10

stall.basis: NEMA17 holding torque 0.52 N m at rated current, Tr8x2 (lead 2.0 mm, d2 7.0), least friction mu = 0.1 -> efficiency 0.463: F = 2 pi T eta / L
stall.dynamic_basis: rotor energy at 10 mm/s (J = 68 g cm^2 ASSUMED) x efficiency into a path stiffness of 10 N/um ASSUMED: F = sqrt(2 eta E k)

load_path.design_force_basis: stall at 1.4 A (driver short-time limit; firmware force current planned 1.3 A) + dynamic + weight

M4_to_plate_only_if_block_NOT_seated.assumptions: preload 2000 N per screw, mu 0.2 (ASSUMED); the block is seated on ZBH-1 at build, so the M4 screws only locate it

load_path.screw_axial_support_in_ZBH1: rev G4: two F6-14M thrust bearings, one each side of the ZBH-1 web (see checks.z_screw_axial_support_rev_g4)

z_hard_stop_rev_g3.not_obstructed: the stop is at the BOTTOM of travel behind the Z carriage ledge: homing and the method-B eject over-travel (Z -12) are at the top; the FFC loop runs on the -X side of the axis (x -26.5..-15.5); interference configs use s_max (= the stop setting) for these axes
z_hard_stop_rev_g3.protects_against: the tool's OWN rack type under its clamp (tallest rack the cradle meets in the model).  A TALLER rack beside the tool (e.g. a 72 mm p300 rack next to the 50 uL eight-channel, contact at s 185.0) is below the strip stroke (185.25) and stays a software rule (keepouts K17)

screw_end.machined_features_specified: thread blank D7 (rolled Tr8: measure) >= 4 mm, square shoulder, D6 h6 journal, M6 x 1 end thread: specified on the T8x2_screw line (custom end machining; a stock screw does not have them)

preload_and_end_float.procedure: tighten the M6 lock nut until the axial play read on a dial indicator at the carriage is zero under +/-20 N, then a further 30 deg; check the screw turns by hand without notching
preload_and_end_float.effect: no free play: pipetting height error from the support is the elastic shift only (~8 um at 150 N), well inside the 0.5 mm disc-spring travel that ends the force-ended pick-up

thermal.taken_by: the jaw coupler's axial float (hubs 0.5 mm apart): the screw is fixed only at ZBH-1

z_screw_axial_support_rev_g4.motor_end: plain-shaft NEMA17 (not an integrated-screw motor) on a jaw coupler with 0.5 mm axial float: the motor bearings see no screw thrust, and the screw's thermal growth relative to the plate (row above) is far below the float

run_current.motor: NEMA17_48: holding 0.52 N m, usable 0.325 N m, rated 1.7 A, rotor 68 g cm^2 (catalogue-typical, ASSUMED); torque proportional to current
run_current.verdict: PASS: 1.3 A gives 234 N >= 220 N; stall total at 1.3 A 770 N, F6-14M SF 2.06; at 1.4 A (firmware now) SF 1.95
run_current.basis: rated 1.7 A (ASSUMED); usable 0.325 N m and holding 0.52 N m at rated current

z_screw_axial_support_rev_g4.M2_corrected: G2/G3 put the F5-10M in the UPPER pocket, where it carried only screw-DOWN loads; the pick-up reaction (screw UP) went axially through the 695ZZ. G4: the pick-up load is carried by the LOWER F6-14M (C0a 1588 N ASSUMED): SF 10.6 at 150 N

eject_method_b.coupler: D20 x 20 (was x 30); motor shelf +2 mm (local z 98)
eject_method_b.values: button position, stroke and force are NOMINAL (params EJECTOR): measure each pipette

params_change_requests.why: 250 mm rail - 45.4 mm block = 204.6 mm stroke leaves 15.1 / 5.1 mm (top / bottom) beyond TRAVEL_Z; a homing overshoot larger than that runs the Z block off its rail. 260 mm (top unchanged, bottom 10 mm lower, still above the plate bottom) gives 7 mm per end.
with 200 mm travel the fingertip reaches z = 7: the pads overlap only the top 11.8 mm of a 14.35 mm SBS plate side. 207 puts the tip 2 mm above the seat and keeps 37 mm above SAFE_TRANSIT_Z.

params_change_requests.requested: state SAFE_TRANSIT_Z applies to the tips actually fitted (10/50/300 uL: lowest 171)
params_change_requests.why: a 1000 uL tip on a 243 mm nozzle is at 155 < 170

params_change_requests.requested: add: nothing above the tool plate top within 7 mm of the plate front (local y > -54)
params_change_requests.why: Z motors (42.3 mm square on the screw axis, local y -31) overhang to local y -51.7 from local z 102; at the top of travel a tool part above the tool plate at y > -54 would hit them

params_change_requests.requested: 4 x 2040 x 193 mm behind the plate below the X beam (local y -13..+7, global z 162..355)
params_change_requests.why: 150 N on the outer tool: plate alone 0.98 mm at the Z block, 3.51 mm 200 mm lower at the tip; with stiffener 0.023 / 0.081 mm. Gantry must confirm nothing passes behind the carriage there.

params_change_requests.requested: board tray occupies local x -155..-109, y -19..+40, z 80..105; chain anchor x 9..35, y -19..+25, z 64..86
params_change_requests.why: both reach back over the X beam top; the gantry cable chain must land on the anchor

first_assembly_risks: Z block runs within ~2.3 mm of each rail end: a homing overshoot or wrong soft limit drops balls out of the block

lead-screw to rail parallelism: screw fixed only at the bottom housing and floating in a flexible coupler; housing and motor bracket are located by tapped holes only -- align against the Z carriage at both ends before tightening
0.5-1 mm static clearances: nut flange to plate front, bearing housing to Z carriage / tool plate, handle to plunger actuator
hand-pipette dimensions are nominal: HP-1 hole heights, V vertices and the 8-ch pocket must be re-derived from the measured pipettes
ejector_space_reserved: x -35..-12, y = handle - 30 +/- 11, z >= 60: kept free for an optional NEMA8 ejector actuator
